evidence: We make experiments on ImageNet 2012 classification dataset, which consists of 1,000 classes
we report top-1 and top-5 error rates on the validation set as measures of recognition performance
we compare with two existing end-to-end, second-order pooling methods, i.e., DeepO2P and B-CNN
unresolved: No seed/repetition count stated anywhere; each reported error rate appears to be from a single training run, so n_seeds is null rather than assumed 1.
n_models counted as the 4 backbone architectures MPN-COV is combined with (AlexNet, VGG-M, VGG-16, ResNet-50); DeepO2P and B-CNN are treated as baselines, not additional models under test.

n_baselines counted as the 3 directly re-implemented/compared pooling baselines (first-order pooling, DeepO2P, B-CNN) evaluated under matched conditions; the paper also cites many externally-reported network numbers (VGG-F, Krizhevsky et al., Zeiler&Fergus, OverFeat, GoogleNet, PReLU-net, original VGG-M/VGG-16/ResNet-101/152) for context tables, but these are not re-run baselines under the same protocol.

n_eval_types counted as top-1 and top-5 error rate; the paper also reports per-image training/inference time (ms) and convergence curves for the ResNet experiment, which could arguably count as additional analysis types but are secondary/illustrative rather than core evaluation metrics.
control_arm left null: this is a CNN pooling-method paper with no attack/defense or intervention framing, so the schema's control_arm concept does not map cleanly onto its design.
